findings.claim: The gateway can advertise an entity-watch retention period longer than the broker actually retains, causing clients to trust checkpoints that may already be expired.
findings.evidence: `ENTITY_WATCH_RETENTION_SECONDS` is accepted for any value `>= 86_400` in `config/validation.rs`, `accepted_frame` returns `retention_seconds: self.config.retention_seconds` to clients in `crates/frf-app/src/entity_type_watch.rs`, but Iggy replay retention remains hardcoded to `86_400` seconds in `crates/frf-broker-iggy/src/broker_config.rs` (`const REPLAY_RETENTION_SECONDS: u64 = 86_400`). Acceptance B requires reconnect/expired cursor behavior to meet the contract, and the runbook tells operators to maintain Iggy history for at least `ENTITY_WATCH_RETENTION_SECONDS`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make the broker retention configurable from the same `ENTITY_WATCH_RETENTION_SECONDS` value or reject values above the actual configured broker retention and only advertise the effective retention.
